originalTitle: Inside India newsletter: Asia’s hottest data center market aims to quell concerns over water and power use
summary: India is grappling with growing public anger against data centers that pose a threat to its ambitions to host the whole world's data.
content:
Hello, this is Priyanka Salve, writing to you from Singapore.

Welcome to the latest edition of " Inside India " — your one-stop destination for stories and developments from the world's fastest-growing large economy.

India is touted as one of the hottest markets for data centers, with several U.S. Big Tech companies investing to set up capacity in the country. But of late, some projects have faced public backlash over the use of water and power resources.

Now the Indian government is taking steps to address the situation. Will it work?

Several U.S. Big Tech companies that are spending billions to set up digital infrastructure in India are facing growing public anger over resource sharing and environmental concerns, prompting the government to step in and calm tensions.

On Oct. 14, Jitin Prasada, a junior minister for electronics and information technology, announced that India will roll out a policy for data centers, calling the country a "fertile ground for hyperscalers."

The minister reportedly said India wants to avoid a situation where consumers have to pay more for power because they have to compete with data centers for supply.

Globally, data center companies are facing public backlash as communities raise concerns over electricity, water and land use. India is also grappling with similar issues that pose a threat to its ambitions to host the whole world's data .

As per local media reports, Amazon's data center near Mumbai is facing resistance from residents who are worried that the U.S. company's facility would receive priority access to water and electricity during shortages.

Meanwhile, environmental activists have been demanding the cancellation of permissions given to AI data centers in Visakhapatnam, where Google is constructing its $15 billion project.

Amazon told CNBC that it is committed to being a "good and responsible neighbor," and said it is engaging with the community through educational sessions. They denied using water for cooling and added that their data centers "do not draw electricity from the local distribution network that supplies homes, shops and businesses."

The American firm also said it "will be a part of industry consultations with the government to advise on India's data center regulations."

Google did not respond to CNBC's request for comments.

Experts told CNBC that the government plans to roll out a policy directive to pacify local resistance to some projects across the country.

It will also lay down clear approval guidelines that will minimize the risks data center developers face from public pushback and execution challenges, they added.

The proposed policy indicates a shift in direction from "primarily encouraging the data center investment" to now balancing it with infrastructure readiness and sustainability aspects, Jaspreet Singh, partner at Grant Thornton Bharat, told CNBC.

Last week, Niti Aayog, an Indian government think tank, shared a framework for local governments to evaluate data center projects for sustainability and to provide suitable locations, based on grid readiness and water supply availability.

It underscored the need to establish guidelines "before constraints emerge," adding that data centers should get faster approvals only in cases where resource readiness, local safeguards and public value are proven.

Experts who are part of consultations expect the new policy to lay down clear and consistent rules, which will also help the industry overcome challenges around land acquisition and simplify a fragmented approval process.

"India does not have a dedicated national policy for data centers, and it is high time that this gap was addressed," Shobhit Agarwal, chief executive of real estate consultancy ANAROCK Capital, told CNBC.

He explained that projects are currently approved under existing environmental and building rules, and every state has its own "variations and incentives."

While the Indian government has been enthusiastic in welcoming the hyperscalers to invest in data centers in India, even giving them 20-year tax sops , regional governments are the final decision-makers when it comes to providing land, water and power resources.

Nikhil Narendran, a partner for technology at law firm Trilegal, who works with U.S. Big Tech companies, said local governments are proposing data center projects in locations that are already facing constraints in terms of electricity, water and other infrastructure.

He added that state governments need to be encouraged to identify locations where reliable electricity, substantial cooling infrastructure, water availability and high-quality connectivity are available, "rather than simply competing to announce large investments."

India's finance minister says market liquidity makes it easier for investors to exit The high degree of liquidity in India's equity market has provided easier exits to foreign portfolio investors, according to Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.

India's rupee forecast to weaken toward 100-per-dollar level even as RBI pushes back The Reserve Bank of India's measures to slow currency depreciation will provide short-term relief, but strategists said the rupee is expected to weaken toward the end of the year and mid-2027, and a 100 rupee-per-dollar mark could not be ruled out.

chineseTitle: 印度内部通讯：亚洲最热门的数据中心市场旨在平息对水和电力使用的担忧
chineseSummary: 印度正在努力应对公众对数据中心日益增长的愤怒，这对其托管全球数据的雄心构成了威胁。
chineseContent:
您好，我是 Priyanka Salve，从新加坡给您写信。

欢迎来到最新一期的《印度内部》——了解世界上增长最快的大型经济体的故事和发展的一站式目的地。

印度被誉为最热门的数据中心市场之一，多家美国大型科技公司在该国投资建设容量。但最近，一些项目因水和电力资源的使用而面临公众的强烈反对。

目前，印度政府正在采取措施解决这一问题。它会起作用吗？

几家斥资数十亿美元在印度建立数字基础设施的美国大型科技公司正面临公众对资源共享和环境问题日益增长的愤怒，促使政府介入并平息紧张局势。

10 月 14 日，印度电子和信息技术部副部长​​ Jitin Prasada 宣布，印度将推出数据中心政策，称该国是“超大规模企业的沃土”。

据报道，该部长表示，印度希望避免消费者必须为电力支付更多费用的情况，因为他们必须与数据中心竞争供应。

在全球范围内，随着社区对电力、水和土地使用的担忧，数据中心公司正面临公众的强烈反对。印度也在努力解决类似的问题，这些问题对其托管全球数据的雄心构成威胁。

据当地媒体报道，亚马逊位于孟买附近的数据中心正面临居民的抵制，他们担心这家美国公司的数据中心在水电短缺期间会优先获得水电。

与此同时，环保人士一直要求取消对维沙卡帕特南人工智能数据中心的许可，谷歌正在那里建设其价值 150 亿美元的项目。

亚马逊告诉 CNBC，它致力于成为“负责任的好邻居”，并表示正在通过教育课程与社区互动。他们否认使用水来冷却，并补充说他们的数据中心“不从为家庭、商店和企业供电的当地配电网络获取电力”。

这家美国公司还表示，“将参与与政府进行行业磋商，就印度数据中心法规提供建议”。

谷歌没有回应 CNBC 的置评请求。

专家告诉 CNBC，政府计划推出一项政策指令，以平息全国各地对某些项目的当地抵制。

他们补充说，还将制定明确的审批指南，以最大限度地减少数据中心开发商因公众抵​​制和执行挑战而面临的风险。

Grant Thornton Bharat 合伙人贾斯普雷特·辛格 (Jaspreet Singh) 向 CNBC 表示，拟议的政策表明方向从“主要鼓励数据中心投资”转向现在与基础设施准备和可持续性方面的平衡。

上周，印度政府智库 Niti Aayog 分享了一个框架，供地方政府评估数据中心项目的可持续性，并根据电网准备情况和供水可用性提供合适的位置。

它强调需要“在出现限制之前”制定指导方针，并补充说，只有在资源准备就绪、本地保障措施和公共价值得到证明的情况下，数据中心才应该获得更快的批准。

参与磋商的专家预计新政策将制定明确且一致的规则，这也将有助于该行业克服征地方面的挑战并简化分散的审批流程。

房地产咨询公司 ANAROCK Capital 首席执行官 Shobhit Agarwal 告诉 CNBC：“印度没有专门针对数据中心的国家政策，现在是解决这一差距的时候了。”

他解释说，项目目前是根据现有的环境和建筑规则批准的，每个州都有自己的“变化和激励措施”。

尽管印度政府一直热情欢迎超大规模企业投资印度数据中心，甚至给予他们20年的税收优惠，但在提供土地、水和电力资源方面，地方政府才是最终决策者。

Trilegal 律师事务所技术合伙人 Nikhil Narendran 与美国大型科技公司合作，他表示，地方政府正在提议在已经面临电力、水和其他基础设施限制的地区开展数据中心项目。

他补充说，需要鼓励州政府确定提供可靠电力、大量冷却基础设施、供水和高质量连接的地点，“而不是简单地竞相宣布大规模投资”。

鲁比奥参观贾姆讷格尔工厂，美国着眼于提炼印度亿万富翁安巴尼旗下信实工业公司的实力 美国国务卿马可·卢比奥在接受印度 Network 18 采访时表示，美国正在寻求与信实工业公司“更密切地合作”，以提炼“西半球”的能源。

印度财政部长表示，市场流动性使投资者更容易退出 印度财政部长尼尔马拉·西塔拉曼 (Nirmala Sitharaman) 表示，印度股市的高流动性使外国投资组合投资者更容易退出。

即使印度储备银行推迟印度储备银行减缓货币贬值的措施，印度卢比兑美元汇率仍将跌至100卢比水平，这将带来短期缓解，但策略师表示，预计卢比兑美元将在年底和2027年年中贬值，不排除卢比兑美元跌至100卢比大关的可能性。
